component.name: Rekindle
component.summary: Read a self-hosted comic, manga and book library

description.p: Rekindle is the desktop client for a self-hosted comic, manga and book server. Run the server on whichever machine holds your archive files, then connect from here to browse your libraries, read in a native reader, and download issues for offline use.
Multiple users are supported, each with their own reading progress and permission level, and a single client can be connected to several servers at once.

ul.li: Connect to multiple servers, each with its own libraries and progress
Paged and continuous-scroll reading, left-to-right or right-to-left
Double-page spreads detected automatically per page
Download issues to read while offline
Reading progress synced back to the server, and across devices

description.p: Supported formats: CBZ, CBR, EPUB, MOBI and PDF.
No changes to the desktop app beyond the version number.
No changes to the desktop app beyond the version number.
Text books are rebuilt: Kindle formats, streaming, page layouts, readability options, an offline dictionary, and books read aloud in a natural voice. Comics and manga turn their pages like paper.

ul.li: MOBI, AZW and AZW3 books, streamed a chapter at a time
Scroll, continuous, single-page and two-page book layouts
Readability fonts, spacing, high-contrast themes and a reading ruler
Books read aloud on your own computer, with the sentence highlighted
Paper-like page turns for books, comics and manga, at a speed you set
Scheduled library scans, read marks and type to search

description.p: Covers show how far you have read, and series show how many new chapters arrived since you last read them. The app now checks for updates when it starts and can install them itself.

ul.li: A reading-progress ring on every cover, including whole series
A badge counting new chapters in a series
Updates checked on start, installed in-app, with an opt-in pre-release channel
Release notes shown formatted in the update dialog
Text PDFs render on white instead of black

description.p: The Discord status now shows pages, not chapters, for PDFs and CBZs in a Books library.
The desktop client can show what you are reading as your Discord status. It is off by default, and Settings control whether the folder name, file name, page and elapsed time are shared.

Turning past the last or first page of a chapter now asks for a second press before leaving it, so a stray tap or a held arrow key can no longer skip chapters on its own. The confirmation window is adjustable, and the whole thing can be switched off, under Settings.
On Linux the client is now also published as an AppImage, which needs no install step and carries its own desktop entry and icon.
